These are figures used to play the Pokemon Figure Game. As Pokémon Duel is a board game, you need to collect multiple figures to create your team of six. These figures have various rarities and can be obtained by completing levels, by purchasing a Booster, or by having enough material to craft them. Each Pokemon figure has its on Attacks, MP, and attributes that can be used in duels. 

==Contents==
[[File:ID-1 Dialga W.png|200px|thumb|Spin wheel|left]]

'''ID''' - Each Pokemon has a different ID, like collectible cards having their set numbers.<br \>
'''Name''' - Each Pokemon has it's own name listed on their figure detail page.<br \>
'''Level''' - You can [[Fusion|fuse]] other figures and metals to a figure to raise its level. When a Pokemon levels up, it can expand a wheel piece by 1 piece. Each rarity has a different leveling curve.<br \>
'''Chain level''' - Also known as CLv, this can raise  the damage of an attack by 1. A figure's CLv can be raised by fusing cubes or a figure with the same ID. CLv also has a different leveling curve depending on the rarity of a figure. <br \>
'''Type''' - The type of the Pokemon. It is rarely used. <br \>
'''[[Abilities]]''' - Some Pokemon have special abilities that give them special perks in battle or when moving. <br \>
'''Rarity''' - The rarity of the Pokemon. EX's tend to be more powerful than commons. <br \>
'''MP''' - How much a Pokemon can move in one turn.<br \>
'''Wheel''' - A wheel that determines what attack a Pokemon will use. Attacks consist of white attacks, purple attacks, gold attacks, and blue attacks. <br \>
'''Wheel Description''' - A description of the figure's wheel. <br \>
<br \>
==Evolution==
Some Pokemon can evolve during a duel, when they win a battle. When Pokemon evolve, they stay evolved, but in return, all of their attacks gain 10 damage and purple attacks gain 1 ☆. You need both the unevolved form and evolved form of a Pokemon set in your deck in order to evolve. 

==Obtaining==
Figures can be obtained in multiple ways. You can buy them in the [[Shop|shop]], get them in [[Booster|boosters]], get them as [[Quests|quests rewards]], and [[Quests|training]] rewards.

[[Category:Core mechanics| ]]

[[File:Field.PNG|250px|thumb|right|The field]]
The bulk of the game takes place on the board. To start off, the starting player is chosen at random. The first player makes the decision to move their pieces. There are two portals from which Pokémon can be spawned on each player's side. If a piece is on top of a portal, the player cannot use it to put a Pokémon on the field. The idea of the game is to either have one of your pieces reach the goal spot on the opponent's side, or to remove all the opponent's pieces from the board and prevent them from putting on new pieces. You have a limit of 300 turns per match.

Each player starts with 6 Pokémon, but as they are defeated, they will go into the backup. You can only have two Pokémon in the backup area at any one time. If another is to go in, then one is sent back to your bench and can be used in gameplay again.

Each Pokémon piece can move a set amount of spaces from 1 to 3 depending on the piece. This can be reduced, however, by special effects from an opponent's attack such as String Shot. You can move one piece per turn.

When it's your turn, you can tap each piece and see how far they can travel and what they can do. You can only attack if your piece is adjacent to the opponent's piece.

If you are unsure how to move, you can let the computer take your move for you, making the most logical course of action.

[[Category:Core mechanics| ]]

''''Plates'''' are used to play the Pokemon Figure Game. They can be put in a deck along with [[figures]]. They can be used at the beginning of the turn and will give your figures special perks. Plates can only used once per match, so you have to think before using them. Each plate has a cost, and the total cost of all the plates in a deck must be 6 or less. They are obtained from [[Boosters|Booster]] Boxes, Quest rewards, or the Shop. They cost a different amount of [[Gems]] depending on their rarity. ==Contents== '''ID''' - Each plate has a different ID.
'''Name''' - Each plate has a unique name, usually describing its effect.
'''Cost''' - Each plate has a cost, to limit how may plates you can put in a deck. the current maximum is 2.
'''Rarity''' - The rarity of the Pokemon. EX's tend to be more powerful than commons.
'''Effect''' - Each plate has a different ability, ranging from [[Double Chance|giving a Pokemon a respin]], [[Max Revive|healing a Pokemon]], or allowing a Pokemon to [[Hurdle Jump|jump over an enemy figure]].
'''Icon''' - The icon indicates what kind of effect the plate has. The purple arrow icon means the plate will affect movement, the gold pokeball icon means that the plate will affect battle, the red icon means that the plate will affect damage, the pink heart icon will affect a Pokemon's status or the Pokemon center, and the blue wheel icon will affect spins.
==Obtaining== Plates can be obtained in multiple ways. You can buy them in the [[Shop|shop]], get them in [[Booster|boosters]], get them as [[Quests|quests rewards]], and [[Quests|training]] rewards.
[[File:MRW I use an attack plate but spin a purple.gif|left|thumb|MRW I use an attack plate but spin a purple ]] [[Category:Core mechanics| ]] [[Category:Plates| ]]

===Goal point===
If you place one of your Pokemon on your opponent's goal point, you win the duel. 
===Wait Win===
If your opponent is unable to act, you win the duel. 
===Time limit===
Both you and your opponent has 5 minutes to make movements. If one player runs out of time, they lose the duel. 
===Turn limit===
If neither player has won a duel by turn 300, both you and your opponent lose.

[[Category:Core mechanics| ]]

Before or after moving, if your Pokemon is adjacent to one of your opponent's Pokemon, you can start a battle. To start a battle, tap your Pokemon and a cursor will appear on any enemy Pokemon that you can battle, tapping the enemy Pokemon will start the battle and the spinning begins. 
==Spinning==
In the battles, you use your Pokemon's attacks by spinning the Data disk. The b attle is decided by Attack Color, damage, or ☆ number. Losing a battle may lead to your Pokemon being knocked out. 
==Attack color==
[[File:Color chart.png|500px|thumb|right|Color Match-up Chart made by [https://www.reddit.com/user/Yokuyin Yokuyin]]]
Pokemon attacks come in four colors: White, Blue, Purple, and Gold. Red indicates a Miss, not an Attack.
===White/Gold vs White/Gold===
When both sides use a white attack, the damage is compared, with the higher damage deciding which Pokemon is the winner.Attacks marked with "*" have additional effects that trigger regardless of the damage outcome. 
===Purple vs Purple===
If both players spin purple, the Pokemon with the highest ☆ number is the winner, and uses its attack. If both Pokemon have the same ☆ number the battle is a draw.
===Blue vs Blue===
If both players spin blue, the battle is a draw.  
===Red vs Red===
If both players spin red, the battle is a draw. 
===Purple vs White/Red===
If you spin purple and your opponent spins white or red, you win the battle. The opponent's Attack does nothing, and your Pokemon uses its Attack.
===Blue vs Other colors===
When you use a blue attack, you will win the attack if your opponent uses a White, Purple, Gold, or Red attack. The opponent's attack will be negated, and yours will take effect. 
===Gold vs Purple===
When you use a Gold Attack and your opponent uses a Purple Attack, you win the battle. Any damage greater than 0 will knock out your opponent, your opponent's Attack will be nullified, and your Attack will take effect. 
===White and Gold vs Red===
If you spin white or gold and your opponent spins red, you win the battle. The opponent's Attack does nothing, and your Pokemon uses its Attack.

==Timing of effects==
Attack effects and battle Abilities trigger starting the player who initiated the battle.

[[Category:Items]]
[[Category:Core mechanics]]

[[File:Deck.PNG|350px|thumb|A sample deck]]
A deck in Pokemon duel consists of 6 Pokemon Figures and up to 6 Plates. The total cost of plates in a deck has to be 6 or less. 
==Recommendations==
People highly recommend having 2 runners, 2 attackers, and 2 defenders in your deck. Runners are 3-MP Pokemon that have powerful purple attacks. (For example [[Latios]]). Attackers are Pokemon with high attack damage, and decent MP. Defenders can be replaced with status effect Pokemon line [[Glaceon]]. You should have 1 attack-enhancing plate, 1 hurdle jump, and goal block, especially in early ranks, because they are useful in case you made a misplay. 
===Sample deck analysis===
[[Poliwag]] is a very useful runner, having a huge chance to roll hypnosis or dodge, making it a great status effect figure as well. [[Shuppet]] is great for surrounds, since it can pass through any Pokemon using a MP move. [[Kirlia]] is a great Shuppet and [[Ghastly]] defence, since its ability blocks them from passing through. If you have a [[Gardevoir]], Kirlia will be even more useful. [[Natu]] is a great purple killer. since it has a high chance to roll a gold attack and a 2 or 3 ☆ purple attack. [[Druddigon]] has great offensive power, since it can go up to 80 damage pretty quickly if your P.C. is full. [[Articuno]] is bot a great status effect and defence pokemon, and it has the same effect of Shuppet. Since the sample deck is missing in damage compared to other decks, it has 2 [[X Attack]] instead of 1.

[[Category:Core mechanics| ]]

[[File:Match start.PNG|thumb|The spinner deciding who goes first. In this case, Lennan goes first. ]]
A Pokemon Duel Match consists of many turns. At the beginning of the game, a spinner decides which player goes first. Both players have an equal chance of going first. The player who goes first gets a MP -1 debuff on all of their figures. The player that goes second will be able to move figures normally. 
==What happens in a turn==
At the beginning of a turn, the player can do one of the following:
# Use a [[Plates|plate]]
# Move a [[Figures|figure]]
# Tag a figure
# [[Battle]]
When a player uses a plate, if the plate does not end the player's turn, that player may move their figures, battle them, or end their turn. After moving a figure, that player may battle the opponent's figures, tag a figure, or end their turn. After that player initiates a battle, the turn ends. When using plates, think before you use them, since after tapping "use" there is no going back. Also, some plates end your turn when used.
==Tagging==
A Pokemon can tag another ally Pokemon to cure them of their sleep status. This also works when you attack your sleeping enemy figure.
[[Category:Core mechanics| ]]

[[File:Field.PNG|thumb|A Pokemon Duel Match]]
There are several types of matches. The bulk of the players play League matches, which is the most competitive mode, where you get ranked for your wins and losses. Occasionally there are Gym battles that players can play against other players to increase their streaks for prizes. There are quest and training modes, which rewards you various items when completed. 
==League Matches==
League matches is the most competitive scene of the game. You get ranked for your wins and losses, so you must play carefully. When you tap play, you get matched up with someone that has a similar rating. You and your opponent has 5 minutes each to move, and 300 turns. The [[Win Conditions|win conditions]] are unchanged. After you reach a certain league rating, you get put in a new league. Each new league makes a new EX appear in timed boosters. 
==Gym battles==
Gyms are events that lasts 7 days where certain types of Pokemon have increased damage or MP. The player gets rewarded for winning matches continuously, in the form of [[Booster|Gym boosters]]. You can revive yourself from a loss using gems. If you win 11 games continuously without spending gems, them you get a trophy of that gym. [[File:Quest.PNG|200px|left|thumb|The Quest menu]]
==Quest battles==
The game has a single player quest mode that the player can play using energy. The story takes place on Carmonte Island. where everyone goes for Pokemon Battles and has multiple hotels, each with various levels and challenges to complete. Like gyms in the main game, once you complete a hotel, they give you an emblem and you can move onto the next hotel. You get more emblems as you progress through the story, and try to get to the top of jewel tower to win the world championship to claim the tower. Each quest is documented on the [[quests]] page. 
[[File:Training.PNG|200px|left|thumb|The Training menu]]

==Training==
Training mode is accessible through the dumbbell icon on the top right of the leagues screen or the training building at the very left of Carmonte island. There are 10 training missions for the player to complete. Each training gives you a deck for you to use against the instructor. Completing the training will give you various rewards. 

==Room matches==
Room matches are like League matches, but you can choose who to play with and you won't gain or lose ranks in this mode. You also have the ability to play with friends if they set up a room and you search their name up in the search bar. You can set passwords to protect your rooms.
